input.code:
def process(wb2012, wb2013) -> pd.DataFrame:
    # group by unique beach identifier: Community Code + Beach Name
    g2012 = wb2012.groupby(['Community Code', 'Beach Name'], dropna=False).agg(total_2012=('Violation', 'size'), exceed_2012=('Violation', lambda s: (s == 'yes').sum())).reset_index()
    g2012['rate_2012'] = g2012['exceed_2012'] / g2012['total_2012']
    g2013 = wb2013.groupby(['Community Code', 'Beach Name'], dropna=False).agg(total_2013=('Violation', 'size'), exceed_2013=('Violation', lambda s: (s == 'yes').sum())).reset_index()
    g2013['rate_2013'] = g2013['exceed_2013'] / g2013['total_2013']
    merged = g2012.merge(g2013, on=['Community Code', 'Beach Name'], how='inner')
    higher = merged[merged['rate_2013'] > merged['rate_2012']]
    return pd.DataFrame({'higher_count': [int(len(higher))]})
input.summary: Compute per-beach (Community Code + Beach Name) exceedance rates for 2012 and 2013, inner-join to keep beaches with samples in 2012, count beaches where 2013 rate > 2012 rate; outputs single-row with higher_count.
